summary: The || operator concatenates two values as text.
documentation: The || operator concatenates two values as text. If either operand is NULL, the combined result is NULL, making a missing component visible rather than silently producing a partial display key.
inputs: refs(id INTEGER, prefix TEXT, number TEXT).
returns: id and display_key, ordered by id.
caution: Delimiter-based display keys are not automatically unique or suitable database primary keys. Use COALESCE deliberately if a different missing-value policy is needed.
scenarios: Build a display reference from an approved prefix and local number.
Combine code parts in a staging report while retaining missing-value signals.
Show a complete composite label only when both required parts exist.
title: Combine required text components
problem: Return id and prefix || ':' || number AS display_key from refs, ordered by id. Missing either component yields NULL. Keep empty strings and numeric-looking text unchanged.
hint: Join all three parts with || and allow NULL to propagate.
goal: Use || concatenation or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
